messages:
Alyssa: FYI incoming ticket from Acme Mobile — they see high latency for a subset of requests and a bunch of 401s this morning. customer says their traffic should land in eu-west but trace IDs show NA fallback. sample req id: req_0a7f3c.

Samir: looking. any pattern on model/route or quota?

Alyssa: They hit our /v1/generate chat endpoint. Model = redwood-v2-small, route=eu-west-1 pinned in their config. App logs show repeated 'region unavailable' before requests get routed to na-east-1.

Alyssa: snippet from customer logs: 
```
2026-03-15T08:21:42Z error: region_unavailable eu-west-1 capacity_exhausted
2026-03-15T08:21:42Z info: fallback -> na-east-1 (policy=auto_spill)
2026-03-15T08:21:43Z warn: auth_failed token_scope_mismatch (401)
```

Samir: ops-bot alert popped for EU GPU pool saturation at 08:20 UTC. tagging @Jamie for capacity.

ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-1 reserved-pool usage 98% (spike from scheduled batch jobs). Autospillover active.

Jamie: we had a batch inference window mis-scheduled — it ramped earlier than expected. That consumed reserved capacity and triggered our spillover. Fixing schedule now.

Maria: the 401s are interesting — are those coming from the fallback region because the customer's token scope is region-restricted? If a token is scoped to eu-west only, and we try na-east, we should return 401/403.

Samir: good catch. I bet two things happened: (1) capacity exhaustion -> autospillover to na-east, (2) their token is region-scoped -> na-east rejects -> customer sees auth errors and retries which increase queueing. vicious loop.

Alyssa: customer reports retries pile up and then they hit our rate limits causing more latency. They included a repro script.

Maria: can we reproduce quickly? Steps to repro from their payload: 
1) Set regional pin to eu-west-1 in client.
2) Send ~600 concurrent requests with model redwood-v2-small across 1m.
3) Observe requests that spill to na-east show 401 and 307 redirect logs.

Samir: I'll run a small repro on staging with pinned region + scoped token. Jamie — can you temporarily open a small buffer on eu-west reserved pool or pause batch job so we don't get autospill?

Jamie: pausing batch now. Also increasing reserved-pool soft limit by +10% for 30m as a quick mitigation.

ops-bot: [ACTION] batch_job_schedule paused by Jamie. reserved-pool eu-west provisional +10% until 08:55 UTC.

Samir: repro started. I see queue depth spike then failing auth on fallback shards. Logs: 
```
[staging] 2026-03-15T08:27:05 region_fallback -> na-east-1
[staging] 2026-03-15T08:27:05 auth_error token_scope_mismatch
[staging] 2026-03-15T08:27:06 client_retry backoff=100ms
```

Maria: mitigation options: 
- Recommend customer remove region-scoped token so fallback works OR
- Pin their traffic to eu-west with committed Dedicated capacity OR
- We implement graceful 403->local-queue behavior to avoid global retries.

Alyssa: customer is leaning to keep tokens scoped for compliance. They asked if we can avoid cross-region routing entirely for their org.

Samir: short term: we can add an org-level routing policy to honor 'no-fallback' which will return 503 instead of routing cross-region. That will be clearer than 401. Long term: we should detect token scope mismatch and fail before sending to fallback.

Jamie: I can push a quick routing-policy toggle for that org (org_id: org_acme_123). Doing it now.

ops-bot: [CONFIG] routing.policy.org_acme_123.no_fallback = true (applied by Jamie).

Samir: re-running repro under new policy. Results: requests that would spill now get immediate 503 with message 'region_unavailable - no_fallback'. That stops retries. Latency for remaining eu-west requests normalizes.

Maria: next steps for support & engineering: 
- Support to inform customer: we added org no-fallback toggle and paused batch jobs (Alyssa)
- Product/infra to add pre-fallback token-scope check and a clearer error code (Samir + Jamie)
- Infra to review batch scheduling guardrails to prevent unplanned reservations (Jamie)

Alyssa: I'll update the ticket and send the customer repro summary + temporary fixes. Also asking them if they can use an org-scoped token that allows fallback.

Samir: creating internal follow-up ticket INF-2026-089 to implement token-scope check and better error mapping.

support-bot: [TICKET] INF-2026-089 created by Samir. Linked to support ticket TCK-5421.

Maria: nice triage. Suggestion: add dashboard alert for 'token-scope mismatch rate' so we catch these earlier.

Jamie: +1. Will add an alert rule after we unpause batch.

Alyssa: customer confirmed they see immediate improvement and accepted the no-fallback policy for now. Closing loop on the ticket once infra fixes are live. :thumbsup:
